verdict.rationale: Temporal ships its own isolated test environments: the CLI includes a local development service for building and testing, started via `temporal server start-dev`, which runs a complete local Temporal Service with Web UI. A time-skipping test server is also documented for end-to-end and integration tests with Workers. However, the evidence never explicitly states that these environments are separated from production data, and it does not document a hosted sandbox in Temporal Cloud. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of isolation from production data, a hosted/cloud sandbox or non-production namespace option, independent or hands-on corroboration of the testing workflow.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: The CLI includes a local Temporal development service for fast feedback while building or testing your application.
This starts a complete Temporal Service with Web UI on your local machine.
Because the test server supports skipping time, use the test server for both end-to-end and integration tests with Workers.
